The bug shipped undetected because existing unit tests constructed `TmuxSession` structs directly, bypassing the exact PID indirection layer where the bug lived.\n6\t\n7\t## The Bug: pane_pid vs Actual Child Process PID\n8\t\n9\t### Real tmux Session Launch Structure\n10\t\n11\tWhen NEEDLE launches a worker via `launch_in_tmux()`, it creates a tmux session with:\n12\t\n13\t```bash\n14\tNEEDLE_INNER=1 /path/to/needle run --workspace ... --count 1 ... 2>> ~/.needle/logs/session.stderr.log\n15\t```\n16\t\n17\t**Critical detail**: The output redirection (`2>>`) defeats bash's last-command exec optimization. This means:\n18\t\n19\t1. **pane_pid** (from tmux's `#{pane_pid}`) = shell wrapper PID (e.g., bash PID 1234)\n20\t2. **Actual needle process PID** = child of shell wrapper (e.g., needle PID 5678)\n21\t\n22\t### Process Tree Structure\n23\t\n24\t```\n25\ttmux server (PID 1)\n26\t  └─ bash -c \"NEEDLE_INNER=1 needle run ... 2>> log\" (PID 1234) ← pane_pid points here\n27\t      └─ needle run --workspace ... --count 1 (PID 5678) ← actual worker process\n28\t```\n29\t\n30\t### The Original Bug (Pre-P7.1a Fix)\n31\t\n32\tThe original `filter_sessions_for_cleanup()` logic was:\n33\t\n34\t```rust\n35\t// BUGGY VERSION (pre-P7.1a)\n36\tsessions\n37\t    .iter()\n38\t    .filter(|s| {\n39\t        s.pid.map_or(true, |pane_pid| !live_pids.contains(&pane_pid))\n40\t    })\n41\t```\n42\t\n43\t**Problem**: This directly checked if `pane_pid` (the shell wrapper) was in `live_pids`. But:\n44\t\n45\t- `pane_pid` = shell wrapper PID (1234)  \n46\t- `live_pids` contains actual needle process PIDs (5678)\n47\t- Check: `live_pids.contains(1234)` → **false** (even though needle is running!)\n48\t- Result: Session incorrectly marked as orphaned and killed\n49\t\n50\t### The Fix\n51\t\n52\tThe fixed version walks the process tree:\n53\t\n54\t```rust\n55\t// FIXED VERSION (post-P7.1a)\n56\ts.pid.map_or(true, |pane_pid| {\n57\t    match find_needle_process_in_tree(pane_pid) {\n58\t        Some(needle_pid) => !live_pids.contains(&needle_pid),\n59\t        None => true, // No needle run found in tree → orphaned\n60\t    }\n61\t})\n62\t```\n63\t\n64\tNow:\n65\t1. The bug shipped undetected because existing unit tests constructed `TmuxSession` structs directly, bypassing the exact PID indirection layer where the bug lived.\n\n## The Bug: pane_pid vs Actual Child Process PID\n\n### Real tmux Session Launch Structure\n\nWhen NEEDLE launches a worker via `launch_in_tmux()`, it creates a tmux session with:\n\n```bash\nNEEDLE_INNER=1 /path/to/needle run --workspace ... --count 1 ... 2>> ~/.needle/logs/session.stderr.log\n```\n\n**Critical detail**: The output redirection (`2>>`) defeats bash's last-command exec optimization. This means:\n\n1. **pane_pid** (from tmux's `#{pane_pid}`) = shell wrapper PID (e.g., bash PID 1234)\n2. **Actual needle process PID** = child of shell wrapper (e.g., needle PID 5678)\n\n### Process Tree Structure\n\n```\ntmux server (PID 1)\n  └─ bash -c \"NEEDLE_INNER=1 needle run ... 2>> log\" (PID 1234) ← pane_pid points here\n      └─ needle run --workspace ... --count 1 (PID 5678) ← actual worker process\n```\n\n### The Original Bug (Pre-P7.1a Fix)\n\nThe original `filter_sessions_for_cleanup()` logic was:\n\n```rust\n// BUGGY VERSION (pre-P7.1a)\nsessions\n    .iter()\n    .filter(|s| {\n        s.pid.map_or(true, |pane_pid| !live_pids.contains(&pane_pid))\n    })\n```\n\n**Problem**: This directly checked if `pane_pid` (the shell wrapper) was in `live_pids`. But:\n\n- `pane_pid` = shell wrapper PID (1234)  \n- `live_pids` contains actual needle process PIDs (5678)\n- Check: `live_pids.contains(1234)` → **false** (even though needle is running!)\n- Result: Session incorrectly marked as orphaned and killed\n\n### The Fix\n\nThe fixed version walks the process tree:\n\n```rust\n// FIXED VERSION (post-P7.1a)\ns.pid.map_or(true, |pane_pid| {\n    match find_needle_process_in_tree(pane_pid) {\n        Some(needle_pid) => !live_pids.contains(&needle_pid),\n        None => true, // No needle run found in tree → orphaned\n    }\n})\n```\n\nNow:\n1. Start with `pane_pid` (1234 - shell wrapper)\n2. Walk process tree via `find_all_descendants(1234)`\n3. Find needle process at PID 5678\n4. Check `live_pids.contains(5678)` → **true**\n5. Fixture automatically kills the session on drop\n#[tokio::test]\n#[cfg(unix)]\nasync fn regression_real_tmux_session_not_removed_by_bare_cleanup() {\n    use std::fs;\n    use std::process::Stdio;\n    use crate::tmux_fixture;\n\n    // Skip if tmux not available\n    if !tmux_fixture::tmux_available() {\n        eprintln!(\"Skipping test: tmux not available\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // session for regression test\");\n\n    // Verify the session is alive\n    session.assert_alive();\n\n    // Capture session details for assertions\n    let session_name = log_path.exists(),\n        \"Log file should exist at {:?} after spawning session\",\n        log_path\n    );\n\n    // Verify the pane_pid exists in the process table\n    // On Unix, kill(0) pane_pid\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Verify the pane_pid is a shell wrapper process (reproduces the bug condition).\n    // Read /proc/<pane_pid>/cmdline to check if it's a shell wrapper.\n    let  use crate::tmux_fixture;\n\n    // Skip if tmux not available\n    if !tmux_fixture::tmux_available() {\n        eprintln!(\"Skipping test: tmux not available\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    // pane_pid\n        );\n    }\n\n    // Verify the pane_pid is a shell wrapper process (reproduces the bug condition).\n    // Read /proc/<pane_pid>/cmdline to check if it's a shell wrapper.\n    let
